_comment: Shipped defaults for MarkstrataSiteBuilder. Nothing here is a secret. Do not edit this file to configure your own site - it lives in the module folder, which an installed module cannot write to and which is replaced whole when the module is updated. Run Initialize-MarkstrataConfig instead: your settings go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MarkstrataSiteBuilder\config.json, and so do the two files you may hand-edit, categories.json and category-groups.json, seeded from the templates beside this one. Values in the override win, section by section, over these defaults. Keys beginning '_' are documentation and are ignored by the loader.
_sharePoint: The destination site. siteUrl is the full web URL of an existing SharePoint Online site (a communication site is the usual choice). pagesLibrary is where the renderer page is created - 'Site Pages' on every modern site.

sharePoint._categoryColumn: Optional. A text column on the pages library that the publisher stamps with each page's category, so library views and search can group by it. The column must already exist - setting one that does not fails the page update - so leave this empty unless you have created it.

_auth: How the module signs in. Leave clientId empty and Connect-MarkstrataSite signs you in interactively and offers to create an app registration for you (Register-MarkstrataApp). Once created, clientId/tenantId identify that app and certificateThumbprint points at its certificate in CurrentUser\My, which is what makes unattended runs possible. The certificate itself is never stored in config - only its thumbprint. appDisplayName is the name to look for, and to create, in Entra ID.

auth._sitePermission: Permission the app registration is granted on the target site only (Sites.Selected): Read | Write | Manage | FullControl. Manage is the default because the builder creates folders and sets page metadata.

_markdown: The Markdown library that is the source of truth. libraryRoot is the LOCAL path to it - normally a OneDrive-synced copy, so authors edit files in place. libraryServerRelativeUrl is the same library's server-relative path in SharePoint, and documentLibrary is its list TITLE (Get-PnPListItem -List takes the title; for the default library the title is 'Documents' even though the path says 'Shared Documents').

markdown._mediaFolder: Folder inside the document library that holds images. Keeping them in the same library is the point: the authoring model is edit-the-markdown-locally, so an image has to live somewhere an author can drop it next to the document. A leading underscore keeps it out of the way - the index generator skips any folder with no .md in it and the publisher only picks up *.md, so _media is invisible to both.
markdown._useWikiLinks: Write internal links as wiki links ([[Folder/Document|Text]]) rather than page URLs. A wiki link addresses the DOCUMENT in the library, so it is shorter, embeds no site path, and is validated by the web part when checkWikiLinks is on. Every generated link goes through the same formatter, so turning this on also changes the index screens. The web part must have enableWikiLinks on or the links render as literal text. Convert-MarkstrataLink converts an existing library in either direction.
markdown._imageUrlBase: Optional. Server-relative path of a legacy image location, used only by Move-MarkstrataMedia to recognise and rewrite links that still point at it. Leave empty unless you are migrating images out of an older library.
markdown._legacyMediaLibrary: Optional. List title of an older library that images are being moved OUT of, used as the default for Move-MarkstrataMedia and Remove-MarkstrataOrphanMedia. Empty means those commands need the library passed explicitly, which is the right default for a site that has only ever kept its images in mediaFolder.

_markdownPage: How the SharePoint side is rendered. layoutType SingleWebPartAppPage gives a full-width canvas with no page banner.

markdownPage._componentId: WHICH web part every page is built with. The Markstrata package installs more than one component - 'Markstrata - Markdown' and 'Markstrata - HTML' - so this GUID, not the name, is what picks one. It is the same GUID in every tenant. To build with the other component, put ITS id here and set webPartProperties to what that component accepts; everything else about the build is identical. Get the ids for a site with: Get-PnPAvailablePageComponents -Page <an existing page> | Where-Object Name -like '*Markstrata*' | Select-Object Name, Id. Test-MarkstrataAccess fails when the id configured here is not on the site.
markdownPage._componentName: Fallback only, used when componentId matches nothing, and reported in messages. Display names change - a bare 'Markstrata' matches neither component now - so a build that falls back to this one logs a warning telling you to record the id. A name matching more than one component is an error rather than a guess.
markdownPage._rendererPage: Leaf name of the SINGLE page that renders the whole library. The web part accepts a strataDoc query parameter naming the document to show, so one page serves every document: /sites/<site>/SitePages/Wiki.aspx?strataDoc=Alpha/Alpha.md. That removes the need for a page per document, and with it most of the deployment time. The page lives at the root of the pages library and its own selectedFile is the home index, so visiting it with no query string shows the home page.
markdownPage._strataDocEncoding: How much of the strataDoc value to URL-encode: full | spaces | none. full is what SharePoint produces when you copy a path (%2F for every slash) and is the only form guaranteed to survive any intermediary. spaces keeps the slashes readable and encodes only the character a URL cannot carry raw. none is the prettiest and the most fragile - a raw space in a query string is not strictly valid, so it depends on the browser tidying up after you. In EVERY mode, %, &, # and + are escaped: & splits the query string and # is taken as the page fragment, and both fail silently.
markdownPage._pageRootFolder: Subfolder of the pages library that any per-document pages are created under, keeping them away from pages made by hand. Only used by New-MarkstrataPage and the legacy-page sweep; the renderer page itself always lives at the library root. Set to "" to create pages at the root.
markdownPage._webPartProperties: Rendering configuration copied verbatim onto the renderer page: theme, table of contents, syntax highlighting, mermaid, math. Anything the web part accepts can be set here, and these keys are the Markdown component's - point componentId at a different component and this object is what you change with it. contentSource must stay 'library'; selectedLibrary/selectedFolder/selectedFile are filled in per page and any values given here for them are ignored. Your override in %LOCALAPPDATA% is merged into this object key by key, so naming one key keeps the rest.

_markdownIndex: The generated landing screens: one home index at the library root plus one index per category folder. Kept deliberately plain - headings and links, nothing derived: a document count written onto a generated page is wrong as soon as anyone adds or retires a document without re-running, and a stale number is worse than none. indexFileName is a PATTERN whose {Category} token becomes the folder's own name, case preserved, so the file, the menu entry and the page title all read the same. A document that shares its category folder's name would collide with the index, so avoid one. homeIntro and backLinkText are plain text; set either to "" to omit it. backLinkText is empty by default because the web part renders breadcrumbs above the content, so a "back to home" line at the foot of every index would be a second navigation control saying less than the first.
_categories: Category display names and ordering. A category IS a top-level folder in the library. listFile maps a folder name to the name shown in the menu and on the index (useful when a folder must say 'Gamma and Delta' for URL cleanliness but should read 'Gamma & Delta'), and fixes the order. Missing folders fall back to their own name in alphabetical order, so this file is optional. A bare name is read from %LOCALAPPDATA%\MarkstrataSiteBuilder, where it is created from the module's template on first use; a full path is read from wherever it points, which is how a team shares one list from a network folder.
_navigation: The site menu. On a communication site the horizontal bar under the header is sourced from QuickLaunch, NOT TopNavigationBar - TopNavigationBar is only right for a classic team site. Note that nothing here sets the menu STYLE: rebuilding a menu's contents never changes whether the site uses a mega or a cascading menu, which is a deliberate choice made in the SharePoint UI. The old 'megaMenu' setting forced it on every run and has been removed; Update-MarkstrataNavigation -MegaMenu or -CascadingMenu changes it on purpose, and a leftover megaMenu key in your own config is ignored with a warning.

navigation._useGroups: Put themed GROUPS at the menu's top level (category-groups.json in %LOCALAPPDATA%\MarkstrataSiteBuilder, or wherever groupFile points) instead of the categories themselves. More than about six categories do not fit across the header bar - SharePoint collapses the rest into a '...' overflow where nobody finds them - so the top level becomes a handful of short group names, each opening a mega menu of its categories. A group node is a label, not a link. Set false for a flat category-per-node menu.
navigation._includePages: Add every document as a child node under its category. With useGroups that makes documents a THIRD level, which is slow to build (one REST call per node) and produces very long menu panels - and it is redundant, because a category node already opens its index screen listing exactly those documents.
navigation._pruneFooter: Remove footer links that point at pages outside the page root. A new communication site ships with footer links to its sample pages; once those are deleted the footer is left carrying dead links. External links and anything already under the page root are kept.
navigation._useRendererLinks: Point menu items at the single renderer page with a strataDoc query string instead of at a page per document. The menu is then built from the DOCUMENT LIBRARY rather than from the pages that happen to exist, which is what lets per-document pages be retired.

_run: Run behaviour. batchSize is how many documents are published between progress reports; dryRun makes every destructive command behave as if -WhatIf were passed.
